targets.bounded_proposition: Slavery and slave trading were established in multiple northern/central Ethiopian contexts around the late eighteenth and early nineteenth centuries, while effective sovereignty in 1800 was fragmented and practice cannot be assumed uniform throughout the nominal empire.
targets.category_mapping_note: Slave status is well supported in specific contexts, while gabr/gäbbar/servant/tributary terminology requires source-specific mapping and cannot be globally normalized.
targets.evidence_locus: Gondar/northern-central highlands; Tigray-Dixan-Massawa route; regional routes toward Gojjam, Sudan and Red Sea; legal tradition as context
targets.geometry_unresolved_note: Later Ethiopian imperial polygons are invalid proxies for 1800; nominal imperial institution and regional effective authority must remain distinct.
targets.historical_terms: barya; gabr/gaber; gäbbar/gabar; ʿamat; garad; captive; servant; tributary
targets.inference_extent: Multiple regional territorial and network attestations within/around fragmented imperial frame; no uniform empire-wide extent or intensity.
targets.language_access_limitations: English translations and specialist syntheses reviewed; Geʿez/Amharic legal manuscripts and traveler source languages not independently re-edited.
targets.law_practice_note: Fetha Nagast and older edicts recognize/regulate slave status but do not prove uniform enforcement in 1800; practice is independently supported by traveler and regional historical evidence.
